statement: PROPOSAL: a record groups the open decisions of the plans of the draft by the part of the draft they concern and the kind of the decision, or the units that leave one critical semantic of one contract open, or the manual actions of the plans by kind, or the open statements of the plans about units they write no resource for by the reason of the statement. It is a view: nothing here changes the draft, target-plan.json, a gate, or any class, confidence or eligibility, and every critical semantic stays open in the assessment. A review of a plan-decision record acts on the execution plan only, by its effect: an answer whose option is what the draft already carries out (ACK_CURRENT_ARTIFACT) frees the steps that wait for the decision; an option that changes the draft (REGENERATE_REQUIRED) or a redesign keeps them held until the draft carries the option (the line of the option in decisions-template.yaml says whether an answer of the inputs file writes it or no answer of this build does), a manual alternative frees only the manual step that carries it out, and a refused opt-in to an API resolves to the draft's own path (the steps of the API path are not taken). The draft itself is unchanged by a review in the decisions file. The one exception is an option that declines a default of the draft (choose-the-size, choose-the-snapshot-count, choose-the-zone-per-server, keep-the-source-rules-and-redesign-a-firewall, machine-type-with-a-local-disk, persistent-volume-for-the-data): the run that reads that answer writes its draft without the default, and the value the default stood for is yours to set.
basis: Records group four lists: the open decisions of the TargetPlans of the draft this run wrote, by the family of the producer (security group, routing, identity, logs, server) and the kind of the decision (plan decisions); the open critical semantics of the units, by the contract family and the semantic (critical semantics); the manual actions of the plans, by the family of the producer and the kind of the action (manual actions); and the open statements of the plans about units they write no resource for (a redesign, a review, a block, a failed model, or a step beside a unit whose draft a converter writes), by the family of the producer and the reason (plan statements). Plan decisions and manual actions cover only drafted units whose draft passed StackToIT's own checks, and only the families whose draft this run wrote from a plan: a family with no plan has none to list. A plan statement covers a unit the plan writes nothing for, whether or not a draft check ran over it; a statement that leaves nothing to a person (a unit the plan does not draft and no manual action of it names) is counted (closed_statements) and is no record. A record shows the review of an overlay beside the open state the engine reached; a review closes no critical semantic and changes no draft, target plan, gate, class, confidence or eligibility. An accepted plan decision frees the steps of the execution plan that wait for it only when the answer's effect acknowledges the current draft; an option that changes the draft keeps them held until the draft carries that option (the line of the option in decisions-template.yaml says whether an answer of the inputs file writes it or no answer of this build does). The one exception is an option that declines a default of the draft (choose-the-size, choose-the-snapshot-count, choose-the-zone-per-server, keep-the-source-rules-and-redesign-a-firewall, machine-type-with-a-local-disk, persistent-volume-for-the-data): the run that reads that answer writes its draft without the default, and the value the default stood for is yours to set. Records of the family "convert" are decisions of the converter's own generators, outside every plan: a CONSTRAINT_CONFLICT (a variable whose consumers' STACKIT bounds exclude one another keeps the source default) and an AMBIGUOUS_* selection (the source does not prove which instance, interface, key pair, gateway, peer, subnet, proxy, URL map or health check it means, so the draft holds a required variable without a default); the unit that owns one is not automation-eligible. options.title: Export the data from the source and import it with the clients of the target engine
options.effect: A person exports the data from the source and imports it into the STACKIT instance with the clients of its engine during a window the business accepts, then checks that the copy is complete; the clients reach the instance at the host and port its credential states. The source and the target engine may differ (DynamoDB to MongoDB Flex), so the export is converted where they do. The plan holds the steps of this option as typed steps: for a PostgreSQL database, for a MySQL, MariaDB or Aurora MySQL database moving to MariaDB and for an RDS for SQL Server database moving to SQLServer Flex (the native backup, its copy to a STACKIT S3 bucket and the import_database call) the preflight, the rehearsal, the write freeze, the dump or backup and the restore or import inside it, the reconcile and the cleanup; for an ElastiCache, MemoryDB or ElastiCache serverless cache moving to a Key Value Store the preflight, the rehearsal, the write freeze, the copy by a client, the reconcile and the cleanup; for an Amazon Aurora DSQL cluster moving to PostgreSQL Flex the preflight, the rehearsal, the write freeze, the copy of the tables by a client (the schema from the catalogs of the cluster, or from pg_dump --schema-only where the preflight shows that it works, and the rows through the PostgreSQL protocol: no AWS page read documents a dump of a cluster), the reconcile and the cleanup; for an OpenSearch store the write freeze, the copy and the reconcile. The decision offers this option only for a store whose STACKIT service documents a way in with such clients: PostgreSQL Flex (for an Aurora DSQL cluster, which has no change stream, this option and the tool of the customer's own are the only ones; the replication of the engine is not offered), MariaDB (the mysql client loads a dump into an empty instance), SQLServer Flex (a .bak file imported with import_database), Key Value Store (the tutorial migrates a Redis instance by the MIGRATE command; for an ElastiCache source, where AWS lists migrate among the commands unavailable for caches running Redis OSS, the copy is a client that iterates the keys with SCAN and copies each with DUMP, PTTL and RESTORE; for a MemoryDB source, where AWS lists migrate, sync, psync, bgsave, save and config among the unavailable commands and the cluster mode is always on, the same client copy runs against every shard primary found with CLUSTER NODES or CLUSTER SLOTS, with TLS where the source has it and an ACL user that reaches every key; whether DUMP, RESTORE and PTTL run on a standard MemoryDB cluster is not stated by AWS, and for a member of a multi-Region cluster, whose page lists PTTL as unsupported, the step says the TTLs are not carried) and OpenSearch (the reindex operation). options.title: Replicate the data with the replication of the source engine until the cutover
options.effect: A person sets up the replication of the source engine so that the STACKIT instance follows the source while the application keeps writing to the source (for PostgreSQL, logical replication: the schema is copied first with pg_dump --schema-only, a publication on the source and a subscription on the target copy the existing rows and then the changes, and the sequences are copied inside the write freeze because they are not replicated). The source needs a change and a reboot to turn replication on, and the target must be able to reach the source. Inside the write freeze the person waits until the target has caught up, compares both sides and switches the clients, then removes the replication. For a PostgreSQL database the plan holds the steps of this option (the initial copy, the watch of the lag, the freeze, the final copy, the reconcile and the cleanup); for an S3 bucket this option is not available, because S3 Replication copies between Amazon S3 buckets and no STACKIT bucket is documented as a destination (the plan holds the two copy tools instead); for any other engine this option is not offered, because no STACKIT service other than PostgreSQL Flex documents the replication of a source engine into it (MariaDB, Key Value Store, OpenSearch and MongoDB Flex document none, and the SQLServer Flex page on transactional replication describes an on-premises publisher and does not name Amazon RDS as one), so the decision of such a store offers the export and the import with the engine clients where its service documents them, and the tool of the customer's own.

options.effect: For an S3 bucket: a person runs rclone on a move host that reaches both endpoints, with two S3 remotes (the source with the AWS credentials of the shell, the target as a provider Other remote at the STACKIT S3 endpoint with a credential of a credentials group, both read from the environment at run time), copies every current object while the writers keep writing, repeats the copy until a pass is short, stops the writers, runs the last pass, settles what the source deleted after the first copy, and compares both sides (the count and the bytes, the key lists and, where a hash is shared, the content) before the applications are switched. options.title: Bind a role of the STACKIT service account to the member
options.effect: A role assignment on a STACKIT service account gives a role the authorization API lists for that account to a user, a service account or a client; given to a service account, it grants the Act-As permission, which lets that account impersonate the target account. A person re-maps each Google role on the account (using it, creating its keys, managing it) to a role of the STACKIT service account and binds it to the member. The assignment carries no condition and has no setting that removes the other holders of a role, so if the Google resource was authoritative (a binding for its role, a policy for the whole account) the replacing effect is not carried: a person lists who else holds a role on the account and removes what the source did not list. The resource is part of an experimental feature that is likely to change or be removed. The documents read do not state how a person, as opposed to a service account, acts as the account.
